## 🎨 Quick Start

The starting point of {tidydragen} is a directory with DRAGEN results. Let's
look at some sample data (tracked via [DVC]) under
<https://github.com/tidywf/tidydragen/tree/main/inst/extdata/oa>:

[DVC]: <https://dvc.org/>

```{r}
#| label: example_input_tree
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Click here"
#| eval: false
system.file("extdata/oa", package = "tidywigits") |>
  fs::dir_tree(invert = TRUE, glob = "*.dvc")
```

We can parse, tidy up, and write the DRAGEN results into e.g. Parquet format or
a PostgreSQL database as follows:

## 🌀 CLI

A `tidydragen.R` command line interface is available for convenience.

- If you're using the conda package, the `tidydragen.R` command will already be
  available inside the activated conda environment.
- If you're _not_ using the conda package, you need to export the
  `tidydragen/inst/cli/` directory to your `PATH` in order to use `tidydragen.R`.

```{bash}
#| label: cli1
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
td_cli=$(Rscript -e 'x = system.file("cli", package = "tidydragen"); cat(x, "\n")' | xargs)
export PATH="${td_cli}:${PATH}"
```

```{bash}
#| label: cli2
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
td_cli=$(Rscript -e 'x = system.file("cli", package = "tidydragen"); cat(x, "\n")' | xargs)
export PATH="${td_cli}:${PATH}"

echo "$ tidydragen.R --version" & tidydragen.R --version
echo ""
echo "#-----------------------------------#"
echo "$ tidydragen.R --help" & tidydragen.R --help
echo "'"
echo "#-----------------------------------#"
echo "#------- Tidy ----------------------#"
echo "$ tidydragen.R tidy --help" & tidydragen.R tidy --help
echo ""
echo "#-----------------------------------#"
echo "#------- List ----------------------#"
echo "$ tidydragen.R list --help" & tidydragen.R list --help
echo ""
```
